columns.name: id
columns.label: ID
columns.description: Unique identifier for the equation

columns.name: name
columns.label: Name
columns.description: Full name of the relationship

columns.name: short_name
columns.label: Short Name
columns.description: Short identifier for cross-referencing between tables

columns.name: parameter_1_id
columns.label: Parameter 1
columns.description: Unique identifier for the first parameter

columns.name: parameter_2_id
columns.label: Parameter 2
columns.description: Unique identifier for the second parameter

columns.name: relationship_type
columns.label: Relationship Type
columns.description: Type of relationship (e.g., inequality, equivalence)

columns.name: logarithm_base
columns.label: Logarithm Base
columns.description: Optional base b for log_upper. If omitted the natural logarithm is used.

columns.name: argument_shift
columns.label: Logarithm Argument Shift
columns.description: Constant s inside log_upper: P_1 <= C log_b(P_2+s). Defaults to zero; this is distinct from an additive constant outside the logarithm.

columns.name: additive_constant
columns.label: Additive Constant
columns.description: Optional real constant d in the affine bound P_1 >= c P_2 - d. A negative d represents a positive additive term. It is independent of the class, though it may depend on fixed auxiliary parameters.

columns.name: multiplicative_constant
columns.label: Multiplicative Constant
columns.description: Optional positive constant in an asymptotic or affine relationship. When omitted, c denotes an unspecified positive constant.

columns.name: variant
columns.label: Variant
columns.description: Variant of the relationship (e.g., strict, non-strict)

columns.name: details
columns.label: Details
columns.description: Additional details or comments about the relationship

columns.name: witness
columns.label: Witness
columns.description: Class that demonstrates the relationship

columns.name: witness_strength
columns.label: Witness Strength
columns.description: Whether the witness gives a strict counterexample to the reverse inequality, or an unbounded asymptotic gap that rules out every reverse affine-linear bound.

columns.name: witness_verification
columns.label: Witness Verification
columns.description: Explicit calculation or parameter range verifying the declared witness strength when literal endpoint values are insufficient.

columns.name: parameter_1_larger_witness
columns.label: Witness: Parameter 1 Larger
columns.description: For an incomparable pair, an explicit family on which parameter 1 is unbounded while parameter 2 stays bounded.

columns.name: parameter_2_larger_witness
columns.label: Witness: Parameter 2 Larger
columns.description: For an incomparable pair, an explicit family on which parameter 2 is unbounded while parameter 1 stays bounded.

columns.name: status
columns.label: Status
columns.description: Epistemic status of this relationship statement

columns.name: proof
columns.label: Proof or Proof Sketch
columns.description: Concise argument supporting the relationship. Omit duplicated prose when latex_proof_label names the survey's canonical full proof.

columns.name: latex_proof_label
columns.label: LaTeX Proof Label
columns.description: Stable \label name for the canonical full proof in the LaTeX survey

columns.name: proof_source
columns.label: Full Proof
columns.description: Location of the canonical full proof when it is maintained by the LaTeX survey

columns.name: derivation
columns.label: Derivation
columns.description: Structured-construction provenance, when this relationship is forced from another recorded relationship.

columns.name: references
columns.label: References
columns.description: Bibliographic support, using shared citation keys such as \cite{key}
